q-49468.binding: The sole selection field completes the indefinite integral in s; the saved integration chain ends in this expression, including +C.
q-49468.source_quote:
We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $u$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {(s+1)}^{-3/5}\,\text{d}s & =\int {u}^{-3/5}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2/5}{u}^{2/5}+C \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{u}^{2/5}+C \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{(s+1)}^{2/5}+C \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\sqrt[5]{{(s+1)}^{2}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

q-50139.binding: The sole selection field requests the general solution y, not the first derivative; the second integration gives this y with both arbitrary constants.
q-50139.source_quote:
Integrating a second time, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (-10x+C)\text{d}x \\ y & =-10\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+Cx+D \\  & =-5{x}^{2}+Cx+D.\end{aligned}
$$

q-50148.binding: The sole selection field requests the general solution y; the second integration gives this exponential expression plus Cx+D.
q-50148.source_quote:
Integrating a second time, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3x}+C)\text{d}x \\ y & =\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x+C\int \text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{1}{3}\,{e}^{3x})+Cx+D \\  & =\frac{1}{9}{e}^{3x}+Cx+D.\end{aligned}
$$

q-50202.binding: The sole selection field completes F(t); the componentwise antiderivative ends in this two-component vector plus the arbitrary vector constant C.
q-50202.source_quote:
To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨{e}^{t}-4,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\,\text{d}t & =⟨\int ({e}^{t}-4)\,\text{d}t,\,\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t}-4t+{c}_{1},\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t}-4t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩+⟨{c}_{1},\,{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t}-4t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩+C,\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $C$ is an arbitrary (vector) constant of integration.
